case_name: Amal Chandra Das vs The State Of West Bengal And Others

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of West Bengal And Others — Respondents

facts_of_case: Petitioner Amal Chandra Das versus the respondents, The State of West Bengal and others. Facts not mentioned in this excerpt.

legal_principles.principle: When a word has been defined in the interpretation clause, prima facie that definition governs wherever that word is used in the body of the statute unless the context requires otherwise.
legal_principles.held: It is true when a word has been defined in the interpretation clause, prima facie that definition governs wherever that word is used in the body of the statute unless the context requires otherwise.
cited_cases: Pushpa Devi v. Milkhi Ram, (1990) 2 SCC 134

legal_principles.principle: The court has not only to look at the words but also to examine the context and collocation in the light of the object of the Act and the purpose for which particular provision was made by the legislature.
legal_principles.held: In view of this qualification, the court has not only to look at the words but also to examine the context and collocation in the light of the object of the Act and the purpose for which particular provision was made by the legislature.
cited_cases: Pushpa Devi v. Milkhi Ram, (1990) 2 SCC 134

legal_principles.principle: When the language is clear, the intention of the legislature is to be gathered from the language used.
legal_principles.held: It is said that the statute is an edict of the legislature. The elementary principle of interpreting the Constitution or statute is to look into the words used in the statute, when the language is clear, the intention of the legislature is to be gathered from the language used.
cited_cases: Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 8 SCC 1

legal_principles.principle: Legislation is always to be understood first in accordance with its plain meaning.
legal_principles.held: Legislation is always to be understood first in accordance with its plain meaning.
cited_cases: Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 8 SCC 1

legal_principles.principle: Where the plain meaning is in doubt, the courts will start the process of construction by attempting to discover, from the provisions enacted, the broad purpose of the legislation.
legal_principles.held: Where the plain meaning is in doubt, the courts will start the process of construction by attempting to discover, from the provisions enacted, the broad purpose of the legislation.
cited_cases: Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 8 SCC 1
